title: HopScore fusion pop allocator - combine p50/p95 latency and path integrity for region selection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current region selection relies on separate percentile signals (p50/p95) and ad-hoc network penalties which produce oscillation and suboptimal fallbacks when link quality degrades. Goal: Implement a single fused 'HopScore' that combines p50, p95, and path integrity signals (packet loss, TCP retransmits, recent circuit opens) into a stable, tunable score used by the pop allocator and tiered routing. The HopScore should improve stability during transient spikes, prefer consistently low-p95 regions for latency-sensitive customers, and enable graceful fallback to model variants (quantized / lower-capacity) when regional health degrades.
acceptance_criteria: HopScore service publishes per-POP score every 10s to routing-config store
Router selects primary POP by lowest HopScore and falls back to next candidate when HopScore > threshold
Canary rollout shows <=2% increase in p95 for test traffic and reduced failover oscillations compared to baseline
Automated test harness simulates 3 classes of network degradation (latency spike, packet loss, partial POP outage) and validates deterministic fallback to target model variant
Operational dashboard with HopScore components (p50, p95, loss, retransmits) and guardrail alerts is live
design_decisions: Score composition: HopScore = w1*norm(p95) + w2*norm(p50) + w3*loss_penalty + w4*retransmit_penalty; weights are configurable per-customer tier
Temporal smoothing: use dual-window EWMA (short=30s, long=5m) with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping
Penalty capping: per-path penalties are capped to avoid single noisy metric dominating decisions
Fallback mapping: HopScore ranges map to discrete routing actions (active, guarded, degrade-to-variant, cutover) rather than direct continuous routing weights
Isolation: scoring happens in a read-only sidecar to routing to avoid compounding failures in control plane
implementation_tasks: Telemetry ingestion: add per-POP packet_loss and tcp_retransmit rates to the metrics pipeline (ingest+rollup)
Aggregator: new HopScore calculator microservice with feature flags and per-customer weight config
Router integration: policy extension to use HopScore for primary selection and to evaluate fallback triggers
Variant mapping: extend model catalog metadata with variant_degrade_map for quick fallback
E2E tests: fault injection scenarios in stage; synthetic traffic generator to validate thresholds
Dashboard: Grafana panels and alert rules for HopScore components and score drift
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive weights could force unnecessary fallbacks -> mitigation: staged canary and conservative default weights; override per-customer
Risk: Telemetry lag could cause stale HopScores -> mitigation: expose freshness metric, require min-data checks before making cutover decisions
Risk: Increased control-plane load from frequent scoring -> mitigation: publish scores every 10s with configurable cadence and use caching at router
Risk: Inconsistent behavior across Dedicated/Private -> mitigation: implementation relies on local sidecar and uses same config semantics; include tests against Private deployment images
metrics_to_monitor: HopScore distribution and count of POPs in each state (active/guarded/degraded/cutover)
Fallback rate to model variants and success/retry counts
Control-plane CPU & API latency for score reads
Error budget burn and customer-facing error rate for affected routes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy HopScore service to staging, run synthetic fault matrix against routing in sandbox
Phase 2 (canary): enable HopScore for 5% of traffic on low-risk routes (non-production customers), monitor 48h
Phase 3 (expanded canary): 25% traffic, enable per-customer weight tuning for two pilot accounts
Phase 4 (general): global enable with default weights, continue monitoring and tuning
Rollback: route policy preserves last-known-good POP mapping; immediate disable via feature flag
test_plan: Unit tests for HopScore composition and weight configuration edge-cases
Integration tests: simulate rolling packet loss and verify planner selects fallback variant deterministically
Load tests: ensure HopScore service handles expected ingest (10k POP-metrics/s) with <50ms compute latency
Chaos tests: partial POP kill + network partition; observe no oscillation beyond hysteresis window
notes: PM feedback (Elena Gutierrez): prefer explicit 'degrade' state instead of soft-weight adjustments for initial rollout
Design comment (Priya Narayanan): dashboard should surface both raw signals and normalized contributions to HopScore
Security: no customer payloads are used; only aggregated network telemetry is ingested
Related research: consider integrating recent EWMA stabilization algorithm from infra-research for windowing

additional_context: This ticket is one piece of a broader effort to standardize routing signals across runtime and console teams. The HopScore should be configurable per-customer tier (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and must respect regional data residency constraints when evaluating POP candidates.
